propositions: User identity differs between Cloud (accountId) and Data Center (name), requiring a pinned contract to prevent assignee diff churn from non-authoritative resolution.
PR #120's implementation used getattr to discover an optional resolver attribute, leaving the authoritative branch unreachable for DC and causing permanent non-authoritative assignee returns.
A UserIdentityModel Protocol with resolve and to_payload methods must be defined with two implementations: AccountIdIdentity for Cloud and NameIdentity for DC with real user-search lookup.
NameIdentity must perform actual DC user-search endpoint lookup and return authoritative=True for resolvable assignees to prevent re-emission of unchangeable assignee changes.

The three-state resolve_assignee contract (value, authoritative, is_account_id) must be covered by parameterized tests validating both identity models handle converged, diverged, and unresolved states identically.
DC must raise BackendAssigneeNotFoundError for unresolvable assignees rather than silently returning non-authoritative values, and unassigned local values must not trigger lookups.
